result.title: Pair-Aware Optimization: Coordinating Exploration and Refinement for Jailbreaking LLM Agents
result.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are vulnerable to adversarial inputs that induce attacker-specified malicious behaviors, commonly referred to as jailbreaking. Existing optimization-based jailbreak attacks primarily employ first-order (FO) methods that leverage gradient information or zeroth-order (ZO) methods that rely on function-value feedback. However, their complementarity and optimization ordering remain underexplored. We systematically investigate four strategies: pure ZO, pure FO, ZO->FO, and FO->ZO, and develop a ZO-FO framework that explores adversarial prefixes through ZO optimization and refines their corresponding suffixes through FO optimization. To coordinate the two processes, we introduce Pair-aware optimization, which retains multiple prefix candidates, conditionally refines their suffixes and selects among the resulting prefix-suffix pairs. We further investigate agent jailbreaking from a more general stochastic-generation perspective, where the same adversarial input can induce diverse reasoning trajectories and actions that a single greedy output cannot capture. Accordingly, we adopt consistent stochastic decoding during both optimization and evaluation. Experiments across malicious-instruction and malicious-environment benchmarks demonstrate that hybrid optimization improves attack effectiveness over single-optimizer methods, while optimization order substantially influences performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 LLM agent 的越狱攻击优化，系统比较纯 ZO、纯 FO 及 ZO→FO、FO→ZO 四种策略，提出先以 ZO 探索对抗前缀、再以 FO 精炼后缀的配对感知框架，保留多个候选并条件式精炼后择优，同时在优化与评估中采用一致的随机解码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多候选保留—条件精炼—成对选择」的探索/精炼协调，以及实验显示优化顺序显著影响效果，可能为 latent 推理中多假设状态的搜索与精炼、THINK 与 LOOK 的先后安排提供方法线索，可供核查。
